name: Methmaxxing

lead: Methmaxxing is a fringe looksmaxxing term for using methamphetamine to suppress appetite and sleep so that body fat drops quickly. Proponents on looksmax.org say the resulting leanness makes the jaw, cheekbones and eye area look more defined, and that the drug also boosts drive for training.

Methamphetamine is a stimulant that reduces appetite at low to moderate doses, and it has a small medical role in the US as the prescription product Desoxyn. Medical references document skin changes, dental problems and a very high addiction liability with long-term use, and some forum users reply to methmaxxing threads describing these effects.

paras: Forum posts describe going extended periods with little food or sleep, with training or similar activity. Some users in a leanness thread say they considered it for reaching very low body fat when ordinary dieting stalled; others suggest alternative approaches instead. This wiki does not describe dosing or acquisition.

Methamphetamine is a controlled substance (US Schedule II; Class A in the UK). Medical references describe dry skin, acne, sores and compulsive scratching, accelerated tooth loss in heavy users, dilated pupils and high body temperature, plus very high addiction liability and prolonged withdrawal. Forum replies often report that the "look" they associate with use is unhealthy rather than attractive.

angle.text: Proponents claim that the appetite loss leads to a leaner, more angular face and body. Medical references also describe weight loss as an effect of the drug, alongside documented skin and dental changes.

lead: Methmaxxing is a fringe looksmaxxing practice, named in the pattern of other "-maxxing" terms, in which users discuss methamphetamine as a route to extreme leanness and energy. The appearance argument is that suppressed appetite and reduced sleep drive body fat down, revealing facial bone structure and a lean physique. [1][2]

Medical sources describe methamphetamine as a central nervous system stimulant that reduces appetite at low to moderate therapeutic doses and is sometimes prescribed off-label for obesity; its US brand product Desoxyn is FDA-approved for ADHD. The same sources document skin, dental and dependence harms with long-term or heavy use. [3]
The community discussion is mixed: a minority of posters promote it enthusiastically, while many replies warn about addiction and visible deterioration. [1][2]

paras: Methmaxxing refers to deliberately using methamphetamine for aesthetic aims, mainly fat loss and a lean, angular face. It is discussed as a form of leanmaxxing and sometimes as an all-in-one "ascension" route combining appetite suppression, wakefulness and training drive. [1][2]

In one long looksmax.org thread the author claimed that after going days with little food his jawline looked sharper, his cheeks more hollow and his eyes more intense, and that he trained for long stretches. The claims are presented as personal experience. [1]

In a thread about reaching low body fat, one poster said that stopping eating was ineffective for him and another said they had used it and became very lean, with people complimenting their looks, while also reporting heavy sweating, tooth grinding, poor dental hygiene, acne and yellowing teeth. That poster suggested a different substance for leanness instead. [2]
Other posters cite the case of a well-known looksmaxxing figure with a history of drug use as evidence that drug use and good bone structure can coexist. [3]

Methamphetamine at low to moderate therapeutic doses may reduce appetite and promote weight loss, and it is sometimes prescribed off-label for obesity. The FDA says its limited therapeutic usefulness should be weighed against its risks. [4]

Long-term use is associated with dry skin, acne and a pale appearance. Skin dryness may lead to sores, and compulsive scratching can result from itching or a sensation of insects crawling on the skin. Heavy users, especially those who inject, lose teeth abnormally quickly, with contributing factors including dry mouth, poor oral hygiene, sugary drinks and teeth grinding, though some researchers argue the link has been exaggerated. [4]

Addiction liability is described as very high. Withdrawal can include anxiety, craving, fatigue and depression, and relapse is common; as of 2019 no effective pharmacotherapy existed, and combined contingency management and community reinforcement had the highest efficacy among psychosocial treatments in a 2018 meta-analysis. [4]
Legal status: Schedule II in the US, Schedule I in Canada, Class A in the UK and New Zealand, and S8 in Australia. [4]

Replies to methmaxxing threads frequently push back. One reply states that former users report that people who use it believe they look their best while others see an unhealthy appearance, with dry skin the most visible sign. Others describe it as highly addictive. [1]
The practice is generally treated as a fringe subject even within communities that discuss other drugs for leanness.

No studies found on methmaxxing as an appearance practice. Medical references describe methamphetamine's appetite-suppressing effects and its harms in the context of prescribed use and substance use disorder. [4]

lore.intro: Methmaxxing appears in a few looksmax.org threads, with a few enthusiastic accounts and many critical replies. [1][2]
